S.text: The elevator cable snaps on the twentieth floor.
You jump at the last second — and survive?
The car is falling at over seventy miles an hour.
And you can't even see when the bottom is coming.
Lie flat on your back, across the floor.
The impact spreads over your whole body.
Cover your head with your arms.
But here's the good news: elevators hang on several cables, and each one can hold the car on its own.
And emergency brakes have been stopping falling cars since eighteen fifty-three.
